slides.0.title: Wine list design and pricing
slides.0.subtitle: A wine list is a restaurant’s calling card and a business
slides.1.title: Structure of the list
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Ways of organising
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Usually by type (sparkling, white, rosé, red, sweet, fortified), then by region or style; organising by style (e.g. “crisp whites”, “full reds”) is friendlier to most guests
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Matching the menu
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The list should match the cuisine and price level: a seafood restaurant needs more high-acid whites and sparkling, a steakhouse more structured reds; every price tier needs good choices
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Complete information
slides.1.highlights.2.content: List producer, wine, region and vintage for each wine and keep it current; a vintage change not reflected on the list is a common service error
slides.1.content: A good list lets guests find, understand and choose well at every price.
slides.2.title: Pricing, by-the-glass and inventory
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Pricing strategy
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Most restaurants price by multiplying cost; a common approach is a lower multiple on expensive bottles to make fine wine attractive and a higher multiple on cheap ones. A common practice that varies widely
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The economics of wine by the glass
slides.2.highlights.1.content: By-the-glass lets guests try more wines at high margins, but open bottles oxidise and waste; a common rule of thumb is that the price of one glass roughly covers the bottle’s cost. Inert gas or devices such as Coravin extend shelf life
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Inventory management
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Stock is tied-up cash: slow-moving wines need repositioning or promotion, and wines that need ageing take space and capital. Regular stocktakes reveal losses and errors
slides.2.content: A sommelier is also a manager: every pricing decision affects guest experience and profit.
slides.3.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
What is the main advantage of organising a list by style?
A. Prices can be higher
B. The law requires it
C. It is friendlier to most guests
D. Vintages can be omitted
Guests find the style they want more easily.
In common pricing practice, how is the multiple on expensive bottles usually set?
A. Higher
B. The same as cheap wine
C. No mark-up at all
D. Lower, to make fine wine more attractive
Practice varies widely.
What is the biggest cost risk of wine by the glass?
A. Waste from oxidation after opening
B. Glasses are too expensive
C. Guests dislike it
D. Higher tax
Inert gas or Coravin extends shelf life.
If the vintage on the list differs from what is served, what is correct?
A. Charge more
B. Tell the guest before opening and update the list
C. Say nothing
D. Mention it after opening
This is a common service error.
